newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein says British Labour could ease strife.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein says British Labour could ease strife.

text.p: A leading official in the IRA's political arm said on Friday he was confident Britain's main opposition Labour Party would bring a new thrust to the search for peace in Northern Ireland if it wins May 1 elections.

Martin McGuinness, chief strategist with Sinn Fein which is denied a seat in peace talks because the Irish Republican Army refuses to call a ceasefire, forecast that Labour would "move forward imaginatively" towards all-party negotiations.

Labour backs the stance of the ruling Conservatives, shared by the Irish government, against a Sinn Fein seat at all-party peace talks as long as the IRA refuses to call a ceasefire in its war against British rule of Northern Ireland.
But McGuinness was optimistic that Labour would not repeat what he termed "the mistakes" of Prime Minister John Major.
McGuinness told a news conference that two bomb explosions near a motorway in England earlier on Friday were "manifestations of what is wrong in our society".
The blasts and other coded warnings that hit rail and road traffic bore the imprint of the IRA, which was responsible for similar attacks on the British mainland over the past six weeks.

"What we absolutely believe is that there is a debate taking place within the leadership of the British Labour Party as to how they will handle the situation in the aftermath of a successful election campaign," McGuinness said.

"I have considerable confidence that the British Labour Party will move forward imaginativetly and recognise the mistakes that have been made by a very pro-Unionist British Prime Minister John Major, and to catapult us...all into, hopefully, an entirely new situation which has at its root... the agreement of everybody to negotiate."

Sinn Fein sympathisers say the IRA will not abandon a 28-year war to end Britain's rule in Northern Ireland until London names a date for the party to enter talks. Sinn Fein says Britain reneged on a previous deal to bring them to talks.

London says the IRA tried to dupe everyone that it was on a peaceful path in October 1994 with a truce that lasted 17 months. Major says that more than soft words will be needed next time for Britain to be convinced that a future IRA ceasefire is genuine.
British security sources have noted a marked scaling-down of IRA bombings and shootings in Northern Ireland over the past two weeks, although incidents have continued on the British mainland.
The last recorded significant IRA incident was the attempted murder of a policewoman in Londonderry city on April 10.
A security source said the reduction might be linked to IRA concern that lethal violence would alienate potential Sinn Fein voters in the elections.
Sinn Fein hopes to capture three key seats in a bitter election struggle with the main nationalist Catholic party, Social Democratic and Labour (SDLP).
